cases.description: An anchor renamed twice, first to second and second to third, is followed through the chain of anchor aliases to the end, as record aliases are: a link to #first, two renames old, and one to #second, one rename old, both resolve to #third, as aliased (§13.6, decision Z2).
Anchor aliases that lead back to a name already passed, loop-a to loop-b and loop-b to loop-a, are a cycle: the chain ends there, and the reference stays dangling (§13.6, decision Z2).

The cycle's near miss: a chain one step short of closing, near-a to near-b and near-b to the live anchor loop, with no alias from loop back to near-a, is followed to loop, as aliased (§13.6, decision Z2).

This case pins an agent's reading recorded in decision Z2 and confirmed by the owner on W4: an anchor chain stops at the first name that is live. mid-a was renamed to mid-b and mid-b to third, and a live anchor mid-b exists again, so a link to #mid-a resolves to #mid-b, not #third, as aliased (§13.6).

This case pins an agent's reading recorded in decision Z2 and confirmed by the owner on W4: a chain of record aliases stops at the first path that exists. docs/r1.md moved to docs/r2.md and docs/r2.md to docs/r3.md, and docs/r2.md exists again, so a link to docs/r1.md resolves to docs/r2.md, not docs/r3.md, as aliased (§13.6).

An anchor alias recorded under a record's old path still applies after the record moves: before was renamed to after in docs/old.md, which then moved to docs/moved.md, so docs/old.md#before resolves to docs/moved.md#after, as aliased (§13.6, decision Z2). The second link, docs/moved.md#before, which names the record's current path, pins an agent's reading recorded in decision Z2 and confirmed by the owner on W4: the record's old paths count for it too.
For contrast, an anchor alias recorded under a path that is not one of the record's own, docs/elsewhere.md, does not apply to it, and the reference stays dangling (§13.6, decision Z2).

A chain of anchor aliases stops at any name that a link's first step reaches, a top-level key of a JSON record included (§13.6, decision AC). In docs/keys.json, x was renamed to a and a to b, and a is a live key: #x resolves to the member a, where #a goes too, as aliased, and #a itself is ok. The near miss, docs/nested-keys.json, holds {"n": {"a": 1}, "b": 2} with the same aliases: its only a is a nested key, which no first step reaches, so #x follows x to a and on to the top-level key b.

check warns ref-aliased for each reference that resolves through a chain of aliases or an alias under the record's old path, and reports ref-dangling for the cycle and the alias of another record (§8.5, §13.6, Appendix D, decision Z2).
